problem_type: Priced paid-card parameter chips hidden, overlapped, or scrolled away by a width-measurement layout policy
symptom: In the Agent panel paid card, a Seedance 2.0 card at the production 390px width drew 16:9 on top of the variant chip (标准 / Standard); at 300px English the variant chip left the card and all three priced chips (aspect ratio, duration, resolution) moved into the gear panel. The previous follow-up kept the chips but made the row horizontally scrollable.
direct_cause: useFittedChipCount decided how many primary chips to show from scrollWidth versus clientWidth. The identity row (model + variant) was one min-w-0 flex item, so it shrank and its shrink-0 children spilled over the next chip without making the row report overflow; when overflow was detected, planParameterChips demoted priced chips from the tail into the gear panel. 712ff9ba7 then ignored the measured count and added overflow-x-auto, which keeps the chips in the DOM but out of sight.
class_root: Visibility of priced/output controls on the spend confirmation surface depended on a runtime width measurement. Any measurement blind spot (shrinking wrappers, fonts, first-frame width, viewport) could hide a value the user is about to pay for, and the only alternatives offered were demotion or scrolling, both of which hide it.
affected_population: Every chips-layout InlineParameterBar: the Agent panel paid confirmation card (NodeGenerationComposer host=panel) and the design-lab chips demo
Models whose primary chips plus identity chips exceed the card width: Seedance 2.0 with its variant axis at 390px, any model in English or with a narrow panel
entry_points: InlineParameterBar computes the chips from splitPrimaryParameterControls; NodeGenerationComposer passes parameterLayout=chips only for the Agent panel paid card.
internal_only_reason: Which parameters must stay visible before a paid generation is Nomi's spend-card domain rule; CSS flex-wrap is the platform layout primitive used to satisfy it and needs no library decision.
invariants: In chips layout every role-derived primary (priced/output) control renders as a chip on the paid card; none is demoted to the gear panel for width reasons.
The chips row never scrolls horizontally and no chip (including model and variant) overlaps another or leaves the card; when the row is too narrow, chips wrap whole to the next line.
The chip set does not read any layout measurement, so a wrong or zero measurement cannot remove a chip.

door_reduction.why_not: primaryParameterChips.ts defines which controls are primary (archetype-derived) and InlineParameterBar.tsx is its only consumer that renders them; both must exist, and neither takes a width input any more.

generality_proof: The chips list is now exactly splitPrimaryParameterControls(renderedControls).primary for every chips-layout caller, and the row's wrapping is a CSS property of the single shared component rather than a per-model or per-width branch. The measurement hook and the planner were the only code that could shrink the list; both are deleted, so no caller, font, platform, or viewport can reintroduce demotion without re-adding code that the structural test rejects.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Render every primary chip in chips layout and let the row wrap; identity chips are direct members of the wrapping row.
Decide which controls are primary from the model archetype; no width input.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The Agent panel paid card is the only production chips caller; its footer segment is min-w-0 so the wrapping bar is bounded by the card width (design-lab-ask-card-in-panel Seedance 390/300 cells, zh and en).
Summary layout keeps the nowrap row and the identity flex box; InlineParameterBar.test.ts pins both class lists.
The storyboard row passes no parameterLayout, so it uses the unchanged summary branch.

recurrence.reason: New models with variant axes, longer English labels, and narrower panels all push the row past one line; any measurement-based policy would again hide a priced value on some machine.
same_class_scan: node scripts/door-map.mjs useFittedChipCount and planParameterChips: each had one caller, InlineParameterBar.
grep parameterLayout across src: only NodeGenerationComposer (panel host) and the design-lab chips demo use chips layout.
Design-lab walk on 712ff9ba7^ (measurement + demotion) and 712ff9ba7 (overflow-x-auto) both fail on the Seedance 390/300 cells; the new code passes.

prevention.invariant: Chips layout renders the full primary list in a flex-wrap row with no overflow scrolling and no measurement input.
prevention.failure_mode: A narrow card grows taller instead of hiding a chip; reintroducing measurement or scrolling fails InlineParameterBar.test.ts and the design-lab walk.
prevention.strategy: Delete the measuring hook and the demotion planner, make the wrapping a property of the one shared component, and assert geometry (no overlap, inside the card, no scroll, wraps when narrow) in a real headless browser.

legacy_paths.rationale: useFittedChipCount.ts is deleted and planParameterChips is removed from primaryParameterChips.ts in the same change; there is no fallback path.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Layout uses the browser's flex-wrap; no third-party runtime decides the invariant.

migration: No persisted state changes; the paid card simply grows a row when the chips do not fit.
residual_risks: Wrapping makes the Seedance 2.0 paid card two rows tall at the production 390px width. The 2026-09-10 v3 user feedback asked for a one-row bar; the 2026-10-08 coordinator contract chose wrap over hiding. Kling-class models still fit one row.
At 300px English the card's action row clips the primary button; that row is outside this change.

The Linux E2E failures of run 37795697410 had a different root cause (fixture credential backend), recorded in docs/plan/2026-10-08-spend-walks-direction-check.md; Linux CI confirmation is pending until the coordinator pushes.
